lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Verify the email and portfolio link if the example-domain contact details are not redactions.
items.because: They should be the live details you intend to share.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality unless an application requires them.
items.because: They aren’t needed to assess UX research experience and disclose personal information.

items.says: Consider whether the education location earns space.
items.because: It may not be relevant to the roles you’re targeting.

items.says: Add the A/B test’s audience or sample size if available.
items.because: It would help readers judge the strength and scope of the result.

items.says: Explain how abandonment was measured if possible.
items.because: It would help readers judge the strength and scope of the result.

items.says: The stated 3:1 contrast threshold is insufficient for ordinary body text at WCAG 2.1 AA.
items.because: Ordinary text generally requires 4.5:1; 3:1 applies to large text.

items.says: Body-text contrast alone does not establish that the entire design system meets WCAG 2.1 AA.
items.because: The stated action describes only body-text contrast.

items.says: Fix the tense and grammar of the opening “Synthesizing.”
items.because: This is a past role.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period or basis for the 23% reduction.
Clarify the comparison period behind “doubled” if known.
items.because: It would make the scale of the change easier to interpret.

items.says: Clarify how the research informed the shipped design.
items.because: The wording establishes timing and outcome but not your specific contribution to the product change.

items.says: The described average recommendation rating is incorrectly labeled NPS.
items.because: NPS is calculated from the share of promoters minus the share of detractors.

items.says: Specify the measurement period for missed appointments if available.
Change “Writes” to a tense that matches a completed role.
Confirm that “all patient studies” accurately describes the templates’ scope.
Clarify what the study setup time refers to.
items.because: It could be interpreted in more than one way.

items.says: Add the measurement period or volume behind the 30% reduction.
items.because: Readers could then understand the basis for the figure.

items.says: Calling the change from 90 to 60 seconds a 50% improvement is incorrect.
items.because: It is a 33% reduction in time.

items.says: Present the route-finding result as a study finding rather than an improvement for all riders.
items.because: The study had 12 participants.

items.says: Calling the change from 65% to 85% a 20% increase uses the wrong percentage terminology.
items.because: It is a 20-percentage-point increase, or about a 31% relative increase.

items.says: Reduce repetition and clarify the relationship between the two transit-map results.
items.because: The bullets credit the same design changes with related results from the same participants, making them sound like duplicate claims.

items.says: Explain the phone-booking reduction without treating it alone as proof of more successful online bookings.
items.because: Fewer phone bookings could indicate that outcome, but the bullet does not establish it on its own.

items.says: Clarify whether 10 patients is the total across both testing rounds or the number in each.
Clarify how the handbook enabled Spanish-language booking if that connection can be substantiated.
items.because: The wording should not imply you built or delivered that functionality if you did not.

items.says: Separate software and tools from methods and accessibility testing.
items.because: It would make what you use versus what you do easier to scan.

items.says: Correct the typo “interveiws.”
items.because: It is an easy-to-spot proofreading error.
